title: The op menu and the op gate are two rule sets: derive the menu from the gate
acceptance: SEG-01 started in `opening` (no poll, no foil): context().allowed_ops -> excludes close_poll and dismiss_foil, and state_summary has a 'not now:' line naming close_poll (no_such_poll) and dismiss_foil (no_active_foil). runner_up: The 'generic' interpreter still branches on SegmentId::Seg02aHexmap (case_open runtime.rs:659, context hexes runtime.rs:2074) and infers the Plebiscite from allows_op("dispatch_research") (runtime.rs:1364): declare a [case] capability in the table so a third segment does not need runtime edits.
body:
## Summary
The runtime answers 'which ops may the host emit now?' twice. context() tells the brain one answer, and apply_op enforces a different one. The menu the brain reads ('Actions, one per line, only these') lists ops that apply_op will refuse for reasons the menu never checks. It lists start_poll while a poll is open, close_poll with no poll, dismiss_foil with no foil, and summon_foil in states with no foil_summoned row. Three withholding rules are also copied by hand into both places. The fix is one tag-level `availability(tag) -> Result<(), &'static str>` that apply_op calls first and context() filters through. A 'not now' line in the state summary names each withheld tag with its reason, so the refusal stays visible after the brain stops being offered the op.

## Description
Registry `show-segment-format-design` / segment-as-state-table: 'An action outside the set is unavailable, not discouraged', and 'when anyone but the runtime shows the table, generate the view from the declaration'. The brain's op menu is such a view, and today it is projected by hand (runtime.rs:2057-2070), apart from the gate it describes (runtime.rs:1475-1752). Concretely, it fails to apply poll_already_open (1499), no_such_poll (1547), no_active_foil (1565) and not_in_state for start_poll / summon_foil / dismiss_foil (1502, 1556, 1568). Its three withholdings are copies of 1623, 1718 and 1743. The technique also says 'when a host action is refused, record why'. Because the brain drops off-menu ops itself (grammar.rs:94-99) and the runtime never sees them, the derived menu must carry its reasons. The summary gains `not now: start_poll (poll_already_open), dismiss_foil (no_active_foil)`, built from the same Result values, so prose and gate cannot disagree.

The rule is tag-level only, meaning a check that holds for every argument. Argument checks (unknown_hex, reveal_not_due, invalid_poll_options, the fleet_lost sign-off exception) stay in apply_op after the availability call. reveal_hex therefore stays on the menu under pacing, as tests/runtime.rs:1584 intends. The change keeps every refusal reason the runtime emits today. The one visible difference is ordering: a wrong-state summon_foil naming an unknown foil now reports not_in_state before unknown_foil, and the tests pin this.

## Flow
- write tests/op_menu.rs: the canonical op per tag, then walk the scripted SEG-01 run (poll, foil vote, handover) and the scripted research/Plebiscite run. At each step, assert menu/gate equivalence and the reason line. It fails today in opening, crowd_game, foil_vote and handover_pending
- update context_reports_table_and_state (runtime.rs test 1263) to the derived menu
- add `fn availability(&self, tag: &str) -> Result<(), &'static str>` that holds signed_off, op_not_allowed, allows_op_in, the per-tag state and resource checks, and the three withholdings
- apply_op: `self.availability(op_tag(op))?` first, then argument checks only. Delete the duplicated checks
- context(): `filter(|o| self.availability(o).is_ok())`. state_summary: a 'not now' line for each Err, omitted when signed off

## Expected impact
The host stops being offered moves that cannot happen. The 2026-10-20 3 h case run shows the cost of acting on refused moves: commit 2aa6c08 records 16 refused start_polls, 14 refused close_polls, and a host who 'kept telling chat the polls were open'. Every new op or state rule gets one place to live, and the menu, the gate and the summary line follow it by construction instead of by a third hand edit (sandbox.rs:738 already is one).

## Evaluation
Claim: for every op tag in every reachable state of the two scripted runs, the advertised menu equals the set of tags the gate would accept, and every withheld tag is named with the gate's reason.
Before: 1 of 7 acceptance cases pass (case 6 only: reveal_hex visibility and the three existing withholdings)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (tests/op_menu.rs plus the updated runtime.rs tests)
Result: better
Gate: architecture (one rule moves into one function; no wire or contract change)
evidence: runtime.rs:2062-2069: `self.table.allowed_ops.iter().filter(|o| self.table.allows_op_in(&self.state, o)).filter(|o| !(withheld && o.as_str() == "dispatch_research")).filter(|o| !(unsealed && o.as_str() == "sign_off")).filter(|o| !(self.arc.is_some() && o.as_str() == "switch_segment"))`. runtime.rs:1499-1502: `if self.poll.is_some() { return Err("poll_already_open"); } self.require_state(Trigger::PollOpened)?;`. runtime.rs:1547-1548: `if !self.poll.as_ref().is_some_and(named) { return Err("no_such_poll"); }`. runtime.rs:1565-1568: `if self.active_foil.is_none() { return Err("no_active_foil"); } self.require_state(Trigger::FoilDismissed)?;`. table.rs:923 test: `assert!(!t.accepts("foil_vote", Trigger::FoilSummoned));`. compose.rs:752: `fmt.push_str("Actions, one per line, only these:\n");`. grammar.rs:95-98: `if !allowed.iter().any(|a| a == &tag) { return Line::Rejected { rule: format!("op_not_allowed:{tag}"), raw, };`. tests/runtime.rs:1263: `assert_eq!(ctx.allowed_ops, rt.table().allowed_ops);`. git show 2aa6c08: 'The 3 h case run (case-3h-464bbf044e) had 16 start_polls refused as duplicate_poll_id and 14 close_polls as no_such_poll, and Malakor kept telling chat the polls were open.' A grep for allowed_ops outside the segments crate finds consumers only at brain compose.rs:745 and lib.rs:1094, sim sandbox.rs:738 (retain) and runner.rs:1301 (test fake), and daemon catalog.rs (the static table, untouched).

critic.reason: Tight write set, real live-show cost, property test makes a wrong build visible.

title: Chat commands open per state and every decline says why, not silence

body:
## Summary
Audience commands are opened per segment, not per state, and three of the runtime's decline paths drop a viewer's command silently. A `!vote` with no poll, a `!vote` for a non-option, a `!summon` while another vote runs and any command the segment does not take all leave no record, no reason and nothing the host can acknowledge. Move commands into the per-state rules, the same narrowing ops and screens already have. Route every decline through one command gate that records the existing 'ignored' moderation event with a named rule. Give the host a counts-only 'declined lately' line so the decline can be acknowledged in-world.

## Description
Registry `show-segment-format-design` / segment-as-state-table, point 4: 'Open commands per state ... Out-of-state commands are declined with a short, in-world acknowledgement, never silently dropped and never executed'. Its failure mode 'Silent declines' says the audience then concludes the command is broken rather than closed. This repo records the per-state gap as a deviation (registry-map: 'commands per segment rather than per state'), and this card closes that half of it. The table half adds `StateRules.commands: Option<Vec<String>>`, validated as a subset of the segment's commands, plus `allows_command_in(state, name)`. The runtime half replaces the `continue`s at runtime.rs:1163, 1198, 1201 and the silent summon path (1184-1195) with `fn command_gate(&self, &Command) -> Result<(), &'static str>`. Its rules are command_not_in_segment, command_closed_in_state, no_open_poll, unknown_option and foil_vote_not_open. Each Err emits the moderation event the function already builds for under-rank declines (1169-1177). SEG-01's cold-open prose ('no polls, no foils yet') becomes data, `commands = ["propose"]`. The state summary gains a rolling 60 s 'declined lately' line, with counts per command and reason and never chat text, which keeps the rule at runtime.rs:2046-2047. The catalog carries the new field: the daemon's no-`..` destructuring forces this, and the console's per-state table gets a Commands column. The operator view therefore never becomes the 'frozen view' the technique warns about.

This is not a policy loosening. Nothing is executed that was not before, no chat text is stored, and the moderation events carry only msg_id and rule, as the existing declines do.

## Flow
- red: update commands_outside_the_segment_are_ignored to expect named declines, and add the cases above in tests/runtime.rs and table.rs
- table.rs: the StateRules.commands field, validation and allows_command_in
- seg-01.toml: cold_open commands
- runtime.rs: command_gate, decline events, and the declined-lately tally (pruned like `refused`) with its summary line
- types catalog.rs + daemon catalog.rs: StateRulesInfo.commands. Regenerate packages/contract
- console: a Commands column in SegmentCard StateRules, a testgen fixture, and names.ts labels under 'Show mechanics'

## Expected impact
Viewers stop shouting into a void. The host gets an in-world cue ('the vote is not open yet') instead of ignoring a burst of !votes. Review and sim judging can count how often the audience reaches for a closed command, which the technique calls a direction signal. A future per-state narrowing (votes closed during a verdict) becomes one TOML line that the gate, the summary and the operator console all honour.

## Evaluation
Claim: no chat command reaching ingest_chat is dropped without a recorded, named reason, and commands can be closed per state and seen as closed in the operator catalog.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: contract (additive optional StateRulesInfo.commands) + architecture
evidence: table.rs:245-256 `pub struct StateRules { allowed_ops: Option<Vec<String>>, prompt: Option<String>, screens: Option<Vec<String>> }`. table.rs:593-595 `pub fn allows_command(&self, name: &str) -> bool { self.commands.iter().any(|c| c == name) }`. runtime.rs:1163-1165 `if !self.table.allows_command(command_name(&cmd)) { continue; }`. runtime.rs:1198-1203 `let Some(p) = self.poll.as_mut() else { continue; }; let Some(i) = p.option_index(&option) else { continue; };`. runtime.rs:1184-1195: summon opens a vote only `if self.poll.is_none() && self.table.accepts(&self.state, Trigger::FoilVoteOpened)` and counts only `filter(|p| p.kind == PollKind::Foil)`, with no else branch. tests/runtime.rs:592-603 `fn commands_outside_the_segment_are_ignored() { ... assert!(evs.is_empty()); }`. The registry-map row for segments-runtime / show-segment-format-design reads state deviation, with evidence 'commands per segment rather than per state ... permits segments without exit handover rules'. scene.ts:145 `return action === "warned" || action === "ignored" || ...`. names.ts:144 is the fallback `R(stage === "input" ? "Chat filters" : "Other", human(rule), human(action))`.

critic.reason: Fixes a known deviation with silent-drop evidence and concrete red-first cases.
